newsitem.title: USA: SEC says Denver "pay-to-play" probe ongoing.
newsitem.headline: SEC says Denver "pay-to-play" probe ongoing.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission staff on Friday said that, while it closed its probe of Denver International Airport bonds, it has not ended a separate probe of municipal underwritings involving the city.

"Please note that this notice is limited to the investigation (regarding) Denver International Airport Bonds," SEC staff said in the two-page letter it sent the city today announcing it is closing the airport probe.
"(It) does not relate to any other investigations, including the Commission investigation: In the Matter of Certain Municipal Underwritings."
Denver City Attorney Daniel Muse said Shea is referring to a so-called "pay-to-play" probe SEC staff launched in early 1994.

The staff is examining whether or not two securities firms won top slots in the city's bond underwriting group in the early 1990s in return for political contributions to the city's mayor. Muse called Shea's reminder about the 1994 probe a "parting shot."
"They've been though here and interviewed tons of people. The last time we heard from them was 1995," Muse said.
"The same allegations were the subject of a state grand jury process and the district attorney cleared everybody of any wrongdoing about three or four months ago," Muse said.
